paper: Collier, Olivier; Comminges, Laëtitia; Tsybakov, Alexandre B. (2017). [Minimax estimation of linear and quadratic functionals on sparsity classes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.00665). *The Annals of Statistics* 45(3):923–958.
problem: y=theta+sigma g; sum(theta_i) on sparsity and ell_q balls.
method: Hard thresholding; Gaussian support mixtures.
assumptions: Known noise and radius in the principal bounds; 0<q<=1 for the linear ell_q result.
regime: Nonasymptotic Gaussian sequence; sparse/dense/degenerate zones.
rate: In the sparse zone, MSE ~ sigma^2(r/sigma)^(2q){log[1+d(sigma/r)^(2q)]}^(1-q).
our_difference: D1 is a classical interval specialization after q=2/K and normalization by sqrt(p). Full-tensor observations and joint-versus-unfolding honesty remain different comparisons.
novelty_threat: Very high: D for a new diagonal-rate claim
evidence: Full text: PDF pp. 3–4 and Lemma 1/proof pp. 26–27; exact Gaussian experiment and rate inspected.

paper: Cai, T. Tony; Low, Mark G. (2004). [An adaptation theory for nonparametric confidence intervals](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503662). *The Annals of Statistics* 32(5):1805–1840. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/009053604000000049).
problem: Gaussian sequence/white-noise linear functional over nested parameter classes.
method: Ordered/between-class moduli; testing; adaptive interval constructions.
assumptions: General classes for lower bound; convex-class structure for principal matching upper results.
regime: Noise precision n grows; nonparametric classes.
theorem: Thm 1, PDF p. 6; upper-bound results in Sections 3–5.
rate: Expected length bounded below by between-class modulus at constant/sqrt(n).
our_difference: General honesty/adaptation theory is known. Here the concrete object is a joint tensor rank-cap class and an explicit o(tau) versus order-tau separation; no new generic modulus theory is claimed.
evidence: Full text: modulus definitions, lower theorem, scope of upper constructions.

paper: Cai, T. Tony; Low, Mark G. (2004). [Minimax estimation of linear functionals over nonconvex parameter spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406427). *The Annals of Statistics* 32(2):552–576. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/009053604000000094).
problem: A linear functional of a Gaussian mean over a union of convex parameter spaces.
method: Nonlinear aggregation; moduli of continuity and adaptation.
assumptions: A finite union of convex classes, with the stated Gaussian observation model.
regime: Nonasymptotic risk comparisons as noise and number of classes vary.
theorem: Theorems 4 (finite convex unions), 5 (affine convex-hull risk), 7 (nearly black sequence lower bound).
rate: Finite-union risk carries a logarithmic class-count cost. For sum(f_i), y_i=f_i+n^(-1/2)z_i, ||f||_0<=k<=n^epsilon, epsilon<1/2, MSE is of order k^2 log(n)/n.
our_difference: Nonlinear advantage on nonconvex classes is already known. Our potential difference is the explicit tensor loading and joint-versus-one-unfolding honesty comparison, not thresholding or nonconvexity itself.
evidence: Full text additionally inspected: Theorems 4–5 and Section 5.2/Theorem 7, PDF pp. 14–22.

paper: Juditsky, Anatoli; Nemirovski, Arkadi (2020). [Near-optimal recovery of linear and N-convex functions on unions of convex sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00355). *Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA* 9(2):423–453. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/imaiai/iaz011).
problem: Linear functional g^T x with x in a finite union of convex compact sets; indirect Gaussian and other observation schemes.
method: Pairwise convex optimization and aggregation; also N-convex function recovery.
assumptions: Explicit finitely many convex compact sets, affine observation maps, good observation scheme.
regime: Finite-sample confidence tolerance; number I of sets controls the comparison cost.
rate: High-probability error <=rho_i on class i; near-minimax epsilon-risk with logarithmic-in-I sample overhead.
our_difference: General finite-union procedures threaten a routine application. A tensor discretization with a sharp class-count cost could subsume the upper bound; no such equivalent theorem was identified in the inspected material.
evidence: Full text: model, convex programs, Propositions 3.1–3.2, and their near-optimality comparison.

paper: Fan, Jicong; Ding, Lijun; Yang, Chengrun; Zhang, Zhao; Udell, Madeleine (2023). [Euclidean-Norm-Induced Schatten-p Quasi-Norm Regularization for Low-Rank Tensor Completion and Tensor Robust Principal Component Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03436). *Transactions on Machine Learning Research*, January 2023. Version 5, October 18, 2023, inspected for the factor/quasi-norm identity (Theorem 1).
problem: Tensor completion and robust tensor PCA; Euclidean CP-factor regularization.
method: Factor penalties representing tensor Schatten quasi-norms.
assumptions: Finite CP factorization; normalization and sampling/error assumptions depend on the recovery theorem.
regime: Finite-dimensional regularization identities and recovery/generalization bounds.
rate: For factor exponent 2 the induced tensor exponent is 2/K; not an inferential coverage rate.
our_difference: The exponent 2/K is established geometry. Our use is a uniform scalar interval plus explicit affine and relaxed-model lower bounds, not a new Schatten regularizer.
evidence: Full-text Theorem 1 and surrounding definitions inspected.

paper: Xu, Ke; Chen, Elynn; Han, Yuefeng (2025). [Statistical Inference for Low-Rank Tensor Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16223). *arXiv preprint*.
problem: Tucker regression: Y=<X,A>+epsilon; arbitrary prescribed L.
method: Pilot debiasing, subspace updates, tangent projection.
assumptions: Correct-rank pilot, subspace accuracy; regression Thm 3.1 explicitly lambda_min>=c>0; loading and remainder conditions.
regime: Three modes grow; rank/sample/SNR restrictions.
rate: Normal approximation at sigma*||P_T L||/sqrt(n); plug-in variance and interval lower bound.
our_difference: Arbitrary L on a regular Tucker stratum versus a special orthogonal L on the entire bounded rank-cap union, including A=0. We sacrifice loading generality and oracle efficiency.
evidence: Full text: assumptions, method, main inference and lower-bound statements.

paper: Armstrong, Timothy B.; Weidner, Martin; Zeleneev, Andrei (2026). [Robust Estimation and Inference in Panels with Interactive Fixed Effects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06639). *Journal of Political Economy*. In press; December 2024 preprint examined. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1086/741623).
problem: Panel Y=X beta+sum Z_k delta_k+Gamma+U; rank(Gamma)<=R.
method: Minimax linear weights plus nuclear-norm bias bound.
assumptions: Rank cap; design noncollinearity; conditional independent errors, moments and weight regularity; no minimum factor strength.
regime: N,T grow; balanced and unbalanced panels.
rate: Uniform bias-aware coverage; beta error O_p(1/min(N,T)).
our_difference: Uniform weak-factor inference already exists. Our target is <L,A> in Gaussian tensor location, with a nonlinear improvement over fixed-radius affine intervals; panel coefficient guarantees do not transfer automatically.
evidence: Full text: estimator, coverage theorem, primitive sufficient conditions.

paper: Choi, Jungjun; Kwon, Hyukjun; Liao, Yuan (2026). [Inference for Low-Rank Models Without Estimating the Rank](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16440). *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 121(553):655–666. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2025.2538272).
problem: Y_it=X_it M_it+E_it; block averages of low-rank matrix M.
method: Diverse projections of dimension R>=r and two bias corrections.
assumptions: Bounded r,R; independent errors/weights; nondegenerate projection alignment; log N << s_min(beta); block-size conditions.
regime: N,T grow; factors may be weaker than conventional pervasive factors.
rate: Studentized block-average CLT without estimating exact rank.
our_difference: Not estimating the exact rank is already solved in important models. Our bounds allow every nonzero singular value to vanish without a lower strength condition, but use a special L and known M.
evidence: Full text: model, bias correction, complete main assumption list and CLT.

paper: Zhu, Yinchu (2019). [How well can we learn large factor models without assuming strong factors?](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10382). *arXiv preprint*.
problem: Matrix factor model with noisy observed entries and an unobserved target M_11.
method: Signal-strength-dependent estimation; testing and CI lower bounds.
assumptions: Bounded entries; rank-one and nested rank-one/rank-two classes; Gaussian benchmark.
regime: N,T grow; factor magnitude may be weak.
rate: Rank-one length order min{1,sqrt(N+T)/a}, a=signal norm; nonshrinking honest intervals on strong submodels under larger-union coverage.
our_difference: Generic failure of adaptation to rank is not new. Our fully observed mean experiment admits a positive joint-constraint separation; its missing-entry experiment has a different target/noise geometry.
evidence: Full text: first-part construction, lower bounds and adaptation theorems.

paper: Cai, T. Tony; Liang, Tengyuan; Rakhlin, Alexander (2016). [Geometric inference for general high-dimensional linear inverse problems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.4408). *The Annals of Statistics* 44(4):1536–1563. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/15-AOS1426).
problem: Y=mathcal X(M)+Z under atomic low-dimensional structure, including matrices.
method: Atomic-norm estimation and geometric debiasing.
assumptions: Gaussian/RIP-type design; noise and geometric sample-size conditions; no universal beta-min requirement.
regime: Ambient dimension grows; geometric complexity controlled.
rate: Gaussian low-dimensional component plus bounded bias; matrix Frobenius error <=constant*sigma*sqrt(r(p+q)/n).
our_difference: Debiased geometric inference is known. A direct Gaussian interval already covers our class. Our comparison concerns shorter intervals for a nonconvex joint class, not mere asymptotic normality.
evidence: Full text: debiasing theorem and matrix corollary.

paper: Carpentier, Alexandra; Kim, Arlene K. H. (2018). [An iterative hard thresholding estimator for low rank matrix recovery with explicit limiting distribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.04654). *Statistica Sinica* 28:1371–1393. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5705/ss.202016.0103).
problem: Gaussian trace regression for rank<=r matrices.
method: Iterative hard thresholding using cap K>=2r, followed by debiasing.
assumptions: RIP; bounded norm; sufficiently large n; no singular-value separation.
regime: d,n grow; sufficient entrywise condition max(K^2 d,K d log d)=o(n).
rate: Rank-adaptive estimation and explicit Gaussian limiting law with vanishing entrywise remainder.
our_difference: Gap-free matrix rank-cap inference is known. The present K>=3 comparison exploits an ell_(2/K) diagonal envelope and establishes only specified length improvements.
evidence: Full text: algorithm, theorem assumptions and limiting distribution.

paper: Carpentier, Alexandra; Klopp, Olga; Löffler, Matthias; Nickl, Richard (2018). [Adaptive confidence sets for matrix completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.04861). *Bernoulli* 24(4A):2429–2460. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3150/17-BEJ933).
problem: Matrix completion; confidence sets for whole bounded low-rank matrix.
method: Residual/U-statistic loss estimation and testing-based adaptation.
assumptions: Sampling scheme, bounded entries/noise, variance knowledge matter.
regime: Matrix dimensions and rank grow with sample size.
rate: Adaptive normalized Frobenius diameter squared ~k(m1+m2)/n up to logs in positive regimes; impossibility in specified unknown-variance Bernoulli regimes.
our_difference: Adaptive full-matrix confidence sets and design-dependent impossibility are known. Scalar interval length for our special tensor loading is a different criterion; projection of a confidence ball need not be sharp.
evidence: Full text: both observation models and positive/negative theorems.

paper: Xia, Dong; Yuan, Ming (2021). [Statistical inferences of linear forms for noisy matrix completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00116). *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology* 83(1):58–77. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/rssb.12400).
problem: Noisy matrix completion; psi=<L,M>.
method: Sample splitting, debiasing and rank projection.
assumptions: Incoherence, correct-rank pilot, signal lower bound, loading alignment and negligible remainders.
regime: Rectangular dimensions, ranks and n may grow.
rate: CLT with variance sigma^2*d1*d2/n*(||LV||_F^2+||U^T L||_F^2) in the stated regime.
our_difference: Strong matrix-completion linear-form inference versus full Gaussian tensor location with no signal floor. Our theorem is not a completion or variance-efficiency extension.
evidence: Full text: signal/loading conditions, estimator and CLT.

paper: Agterberg, Joshua; Zhang, Anru R. (2024). [Statistical Inference for Low-Rank Tensors: Heteroskedasticity, Subgaussianity, and Applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06381). *arXiv preprint*.
problem: Tucker signal plus independent heteroskedastic sub-Gaussian noise.
method: HOOI with initialization; perturbation expansions; estimated variances.
assumptions: Incoherence/conditioning; SNR lambda/sigma >=constant*p^(3/4)*sqrt(log p); further rank and entry alignment restrictions.
regime: Comparable mode sizes p grow.
rate: Row expansion, entrywise studentized CLT, confidence intervals and efficiency results.
our_difference: Tensor inference and noise heterogeneity are known. Our theorem removes a minimum signal requirement in a narrower loading/experiment, and does not claim heteroskedastic adaptivity.
evidence: Full text: expansion, CLT, feasible inference and lower-bound statements.

paper: Xia, Dong; Zhang, Anru; Zhou, Yuchen (2022). [Inference for Low-rank Tensors---No Need to Debias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.14844). *The Annals of Statistics* 50(2):1220–1245. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/21-AOS2146).
problem: Tucker PCA/regression; subspaces, rank-one entries and linear forms.
method: Two iterations of alternating minimization; no explicit debiasing.
assumptions: Accurate initializer; conditioning and rank restrictions; strong enough SNR.
regime: PCA: (pr)^(3/4)/(lambda/sigma)->0, r^3/p->0 under bounded conditioning.
rate: Normal limits for scaled subspace losses; regression analogue with explicit n/SNR remainders.
our_difference: Strong-signal tensor subspace/function inference versus uniform coverage at the zero tensor and all lower-rank strata. Their strong-signal efficiency is not dominated.
evidence: Full text: PCA and regression theorem statements and initialization conditions.

paper: Carpentier, Alexandra; Nickl, Richard (2015). [On signal detection and confidence sets for low rank inference problems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03829). *Electronic Journal of Statistics* 9(2):2675–2688. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/15-EJS1087).
problem: Gaussian matrix trace regression; low-rank testing and confidence sets.
method: Detection lower/upper bounds and reduction from confidence sets.
assumptions: Gaussian isotropic design/noise; rank restrictions; PSD constraint changes conclusions.
regime: d,n grow; small-rank alternatives.
theorem: Thm 1 and confidence-set consequences; PDF pp. 4–9.
rate: Frobenius detection radius min{sqrt(d/n),n^(-1/4)}; nuclear radius has sqrt(k) factor.
our_difference: Testing controls rank adaptation and norm choice already. Our mixture computes an explicit functional cost of enlarging simultaneous tensor constraints to one unfolding.
evidence: Full text: metric-specific detection and confidence-set results.

paper: Wasserman, Larry; Ramdas, Aaditya; Balakrishnan, Sivaraman (2020). [Universal inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11436). *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences* 117(29):16880–16890. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1922664117).
problem: Likelihood models, including irregular parameter spaces.
method: Split likelihood ratio; invert tests and profile nuisance parameters.
assumptions: Correct likelihood and independent split; finite-sample validity needs no smooth manifold.
regime: Finite sample; regular-model diameter theorem separately requires fixed dimension and a consistent pilot.
rate: Coverage >=1-alpha exactly; regular diameter O_p(sqrt(log(1/alpha)/n)).
our_difference: Generic finite-sample validity is available. Our added target is explicit deterministic length and a separation; universal coverage alone is not a contribution.
evidence: Full text HTML: theorem statements, proof of coverage, profiling and safe bounds.

paper: Bykhovskaya, Anna; Gorin, Vadim; Sodin, Sasha (2025). [How weak are weak factors? Uniform inference for signal strength in signal plus noise models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18554). *arXiv preprint*.
problem: Spiked matrix factor/covariance/Wigner/CCA models; signal strengths.
method: Transition-aware random-matrix distribution approximations.
assumptions: Specified noise models; finite spikes; distinct fixed others in the cited critical theorem.
regime: Thm 4.6: one spike theta_c+N^(-1/3)h; eigenvalue scale N^(-2/3).
rate: Uniform treatment connecting subcritical/critical behavior to supercritical Gaussian inference.
our_difference: Uniform inference near critical matrix signal strengths is already studied. Our target is a signed tensor contrast and the comparison is parameter-class honesty, not spike magnitude.
evidence: Full text: critical transition theorem and restrictions.

paper: Cai, Changxiao; Poor, H. Vincent; Chen, Yuxin (2023). [Uncertainty Quantification for Nonconvex Tensor Completion: Confidence Intervals, Heteroscedasticity and Optimality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08580). *IEEE Transactions on Information Theory* 69(1):407–452. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2022.3205781).
problem: Symmetric order-three CP tensor completion from Bernoulli entries.
method: Spectral initialization and nonconvex gradient estimation; residual variance estimation.
assumptions: Incoherent, well-conditioned CP factors; sample/SNR restrictions; target-entry strength condition; independent heteroskedastic noise.
regime: Tensor size grows; fixed or controlled rank.
rate: Studentized entry/factor CLTs and confidence intervals; Gaussian unbiased-estimator variance lower bounds.
our_difference: Entry/factor intervals in tensor completion are known under recovery conditions. Here observation is complete, noise known, target a high-rank loading, and actual tensor rank may be arbitrarily weak.
evidence: Full 2020 author manuscript: assumptions, CI theorems and scope of lower bound; 2023 journal metadata verified.

paper: Ke, Baofang; Song, Zihao; Zhao, Weihua; Wang, Lei (2026). [Efficient Inference for Low-rank Regression via Covariance-Weighted Projection](https://www3.stat.sinica.edu.tw/statistica/fp/SS-2026-0222.html). *Statistica Sinica*. Accepted preprint, updated September 8, 2026. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5705/ss.202026.0222).
problem: Structured regression with nonidentity design covariance; Tucker specialization.
method: Covariance-weighted tangent projection and feasible one-step inference.
assumptions: C1 embedded manifold; independent consistent pilot; covariance/projection rates; Tucker Assumption 5 imposes lambda>=c>0.
regime: General manifold theorem plus growing-dimensional Tucker conditions.
rate: Normal variance sigma^2*||Phi(L)||_Sigma^2/N; local minimax length lower bound.
our_difference: Covariance-aware efficient inference on regular low-rank manifolds versus special-loading finite-sample union honesty. Unknown covariance and oracle efficiency remain outside our theorem.
evidence: Full PDF read online; accepted preprint updated 2026-09-08.
